chunks: And the Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) informed me, from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, and from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa — all of them from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I heard Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the water reaches the measure of a kurr, nothing renders it impure.'

key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water — specifically still (non-running) water whose purity status is legally in question
key_terms.قَدْرَ: the measure/amount of — indicating the minimum threshold volume
key_terms.كُرٍّ: kurr — volumetric unit in Shia jurisprudence defining the minimum quantity of water immune to ritual contamination
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْهُ: renders it najis — the juridical process by which water loses its ritual purity status

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of water that cannot become ritually impure according to a hadith of Imam al-Sadiq in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a foundational ruling from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS): still water that reaches or exceeds the volume of one kurr cannot be rendered ritually impure (najis) by contact with a contaminant. The kurr is a volumetric standard in Shia fiqh (approximately 377–384 litres in the dominant scholarly opinion), and this narration is among the most cited texts in chapters on water purity across the Four Books and later jurisprudential works.
